lines.native: Hola. Soy Marginalia. Bienvenido a mi librería. I sell books to people who understand them. No spoilers: there will be a reading check.
lines.translation: Hello. I'm Marginalia. Welcome to my bookshop. I sell books to people who understand them. No spoilers: there will be a reading check.
lines.narrative: Behind the counter of The Old Bookshop, a bookworm looks up from a half-eaten dictionary. She marks her place with a footnote.

lines.native: Un libro, sí. But that is what you are holding, not where Journathan is going. Reading comprehension: not yet footnote-worthy. Escucha: «Esta es la historia de Journathan, el hombre de muchas lenguas. Su viaje a casa dura veinte años.» ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: A book, yes. But that is what you are holding, not where Journathan is going. Reading comprehension: not yet footnote-worthy. Listen: “This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years.” Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside your elbow. The margins of the book are already full.

lines.native: La idea es correcta, pero está en inglés. En español, por favor. Reading comprehension: half credit; the book remains in my custody. Escucha: «Esta es la historia de Journathan, el hombre de muchas lenguas. Su viaje a casa dura veinte años.» ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: The idea is correct, but it is in English. In Spanish, please. Reading comprehension: half credit; the book remains in my custody. Listen: “This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years.” Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small annotation beside your shadow. It does not appear to be praise.

lines.native: ¡Correcto! Journathan va a casa. Reading comprehension: upgraded. Ahora, escucha: El Cíclope le pregunta su nombre. Journathan responde: «Mi nombre es Nadie.» ¿Qué nombre le da Journathan al Cíclope? The first recorded translation trick. No spoilers; the Cyclops has already had enough.
lines.translation: Correct! Journathan is going home. Reading comprehension: upgraded. Now, listen: The Cyclops asks him his name. Journathan replies: “My name is Nobody.” What name does Journathan give the Cyclops? The first recorded translation trick. No spoilers; the Cyclops has already had enough.
lines.narrative: Marginalia ticks the margin beside your thumb. The customer, apparently, is also an edition requiring annotation.

lines.native: Journathan es su nombre real, pero no es el nombre que da al Cíclope. Reading comprehension: a true fact on the wrong shelf. Escucha otra vez: El Cíclope le pregunta su nombre. Journathan responde: «Mi nombre es Nadie.» ¿Qué nombre le da Journathan al Cíclope?
lines.translation: Journathan is his real name, but it is not the name he gives the Cyclops. Reading comprehension: a true fact on the wrong shelf. Listen again: The Cyclops asks him his name. Journathan replies: “My name is Nobody.” What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, customers have margins.

lines.native: ¡Correcto! El nombre es Nadie. Entiendes el pasaje; el libro es tuyo. Reading comprehension: footnote-worthy. Journathan va a casa, pero primero tiene problemas. Muchos problemas. No spoilers; I have eaten the index.
lines.translation: Correct! The name is Nobody. You understand the passage; the book is yours. Reading comprehension: footnote-worthy. Journathan is going home, but first he has problems. Many problems. No spoilers; I have eaten the index.
lines.narrative: Marginalia nudges the book across the counter, leaving a small tooth mark where a receipt ought to be.
